judged_text: The rewritten public members action feeds params[:limit] and params[:offset] straight into the SQL limit/offset with no non-negative validation. Any user can request /groups/:name/members?limit=-1 (or a negative offset) and trigger a 500 from PostgreSQL's "LIMIT must not be negative" instead of a 4xx — a hole the rewrite extends from automatic groups to every group.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and feeds them directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no non-negative clamping/validation. Negative values (e.g. `limit=-1` or `offset=-5`) can produce SQL like `LIMIT -1` / `OFFSET -5`, which PostgreSQL rejects (500). The rewrite also expands this risk from only automatic groups (previously the only case applying limit/offset) to all groups.
